---
title: "Query Expansion"
description: "A retrieval technique that adds related terms to a search query to improve matching with relevant documents."
term: "Query Expansion"
letter: "Q"
category: "Information Retrieval"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Query expansion adds likely related words or phrases to a search request.
This can help when a user's wording differs from the words used in useful
documents.

## Technical explanation

Expansion may use synonyms, domain vocabularies, relevance feedback, or
language models to produce additional query terms. In lexical retrieval,
the expanded query is matched against document terms; in hybrid systems,
expansion can also affect semantic retrieval or reranking.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Expansion can improve recall when queries are short, ambiguous, or use
different terminology from the document collection. Poor expansions can
introduce noise, change intent, and reduce precision, so the method needs
evaluation on representative queries.

## How it works

The system identifies candidate related terms and combines them with the
original query, often assigning different weights. Feedback-based methods
derive terms from initially retrieved documents; model-generated expansions
should be constrained and tested to avoid unsupported additions.

## Practical example

A search for “car repair” might be expanded with “automotive service” and
“vehicle maintenance” before retrieval. The original query should remain
available so the system does not lose the user's intended wording.

## Common misconceptions

- More query terms do not always improve results; irrelevant terms can hurt
  ranking.
- Generated expansions are suggestions, not evidence that the added terms
  reflect the user's intent.
